slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: most revenue comes from café wholesale [S5]
Opportunity: café fans already love the product [R1]
Solution: Fuel the Morning turns café fans into home buyers
Goal: 1,500 DTC orders in 45 days [O1]
slides.notes: Open with the problem and the goal.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Small-batch granola sold to cafés across Austin [S5]
Three flavors, sold in 12 oz bags [S5]
Clean-label positioning versus mass brands [S1]
slides.notes: Hold up a printed product card.

slides.title: The Company & Its Position
bullets: Founded in Austin; wholesale-first growth [S5]
Positioned premium-craft versus mass granola [S1]
Competitors compete on price, not freshness [S2]
slides.notes: Point to the white space on the map.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1: 1,500 DTC orders [O1]
O2: 3,000 new email subscribers [O2]
O3: +10 points aided awareness in Austin [O3]
slides.notes: Each objective returns on the KPI slide.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: Primary: Café Regulars, 25-40, buy coffee out often [R1]
Secondary: Busy Parents, 30-45, need fast breakfasts [R2]
Both segments discover food on Instagram first [R2]
slides.notes: Introduce the two personas by name.

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Survey of 50 Austin adults, Nov 7-9 [R1]
Three customer interviews, Nov 8 [R3]
Competitor audit of four granola brands [S2]
slides.notes: Show the survey chart to the judge.

slides.title: Insights → Campaign Decisions
bullets: Café fans want the product at home [R1] → café QR program
Instagram leads discovery [R2] → Instagram-first paid media
Starter bundles lower risk [R3] → week-6 bundle drop

slides.title: Fuel the Morning: Strategy
bullets: Fuel the Morning turns the café counter into a store [R1]
Instagram-first because discovery starts there [R2]
Bundles convert first-time buyers [R3]
